comments.content: This looks like an accidental corruption of the documentation example: `{{ outputs.output_values.²}}` is invalid Pebble syntax and will break the example. It should likely be `{{ outputs.output_values.values.taskrun_data }}`.
The example code contains a stray `\n\" +` inside the YAML string (`"  - id: fail\\n\" +\n"`), which will produce invalid YAML in the rendered example. Remove the leftover concatenation artifact.

`this.conditions.getExpression()` is used directly without rendering. If the conditions property itself contains Pebble expressions (e.g. built from inputs), they won't be resolved before parsing as JSON. Consider using `runContext.render(this.conditions).asList(String.class)` or rendering the expression first.
The log message has two placeholders `{}` but only one argument is passed (`s`); `renderer` is silently ignored. Either remove the extra placeholder or pass `renderer` as an argument.
`failed` is an `AtomicInteger`; string concatenation will print the object's toString (e.g. `java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger@...`) rather than the count. Use `failed.get()`.
`runContext.render(errorMessage)` will throw NPE when `errorMessage` is null (the common case). Guard with a null check or use `Optional.ofNullable(errorMessage).map(...)`.

`isFalsy` returns false for `null`, which is inconsistent with the semantics used by `Assert`: a null renderer should be treated as falsy (assertion failed). Consider `condition == null || FALSE_VALUES.contains(condition)`.
Missing trailing newline at end of file.
